notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its regular and special meetings, January to June 1976, from volume 32 of the San Francisco Public Library's deposit at the Internet Archive (32minutesofsanfran1976sa). Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false, and every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the minutes state stood on or occupied the property; dated past facts the minutes state about a building; and landmark actions. A proposal on its own is not a finding. A Board of Supervisors action the minutes report without its own date is framed 'by' the date of the meeting that reported it. The minutes name applicants, owners, attorneys, objectors, commissioners and staff throughout; the reader spec (in research/sources/sf-planning-commission-minutes.md, under Reader spec) barred all of them from every field, and kept companies, institutions, named buildings and architects.

coverage.remaining: Every page of volume 32 (32minutesofsanfran1976sa, January-June 1976) was read. Next: volume 33 (33minutesofsanfran1976san, July-December 1976), then 34-39 (1977-1980) and 40-58 (1994-2005). coverage.note: 519 OCR pages with text out of 582 viewer pages (584 scanned leaves), read in one session by a single reader with no sub-agents; 28 meetings (19 regular, 9 special or summary) from 7 January to 24 June 1976, each dated from its own header. The new Mayor's Commission took office at the special meeting of 3 February. 114 findings: 57 statements of what stood on or occupied a property, 47 decisions, 6 dated past facts, 4 landmark actions. Every quote was re-anchored mechanically against its own page (114 of 114). 69 resolved: 54 by the EAS join on a printed number, 15 by hand — 2 by the record's own block and lot (7 Vulcan Stairway is now 60 Lower Terrace; 65 Belgrave re-lotted), 3 by lot area (the two Sacramento Street lots at Laurel, 41.25 x 62 feet each, are the 5,115-square-foot parcel of 3490 Sacramento, built 1977), 3 past an EAS stray (318 Laurel filed on another lot), 7 by name on a building a page already carries. 65 published on 43 pages, 13 of them seeded; 4 declined (2 already on the page from earlier volumes, 1 a speaker's unsupported claim, 1 a duplicate). Four conflicts stated in unknowns: 909 Hyde's three building dates, 525 Golden Gate's 1958 against 1959, 3255 Broderick's 1929 against the roll's 1928, and 827 Guerrero's 1976 care home against a 1978 opening. The half-year's distinctive matters: the Bush Street Temple and Geary Theater landmark votes; the Atherton House club refused; the Lilienthal-Orville Pratt House office refused; the 316-318 Laurel psychiatrists' offices refused under discretionary review on C-2 land, and the Sacramento Street corner lots steered into one building with parking; St. Francis Memorial Hospital's outpatient addition approved 5-2 after six hearings; the tree-protection ordinance; and the interim residential rezoning of the whole city initiated on 20 May.
